 In The High Court At Calcutta

 Appellate Side

The Hon'ble Justice Ananya Bandyopadhyay
 Fma 331 of 2019
 Mor Selim Sk.
 Versus
 The National Insurance Company Ltd. & Anr.
For the Appellant : Mr. Amit Ranjan Roy

For the Respondent No.1/ : Mr. Saibalendu Bhowmick
Insurance co.
Heard on & Judgment on : 10th June, 2025.
Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J:
1.
The instant appeal was heard earlier and judgment was reserved.

However, the matter was listed under the heading "For Hearing"
for further clarification.
2. The Learned Advocates representing the respective parties are present.

3. The instant appeal had been filed against the judgment and award dated 29th September, 2018 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Howrah in M.A.C. Case No. 321 of 2013.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Howrah
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. An application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act had been filed by the injured victim claiming compensation for having sustained 80% physical disability out of an accident incurred by him with the involvement of the offending vehicle being a bus bearing registration No. WB-15 A/5417 which rashly and negligently applied the brake.
Due to sudden inertia, the victim was pushed out of the gate of the bus and suffered severe injuries on his waist and left leg which had to be amputated causing permanent disablement.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate representing the appellant/claimant submitted the learned Tribunal erroneously considered the income of the victim to be Rs. 15,000/- per annum in spite of the claim of the victim of earning 300 to 400 rupees per day working as a "jari worker".
Moreover, 40% of compensation towards the element of future prospect was not granted and a modicum amount of Rs. 5000/- was granted towards pain and suffering.

6. The learned Advocate representing the respondent No.1/Insurance Company submitted the learned Tribunal erroneously considered the multiplier to be 18 instead of 16 since the age of the victim at the time of the accident was 32.

The Learned Advocate representing the respondent No.1/insurance company further submitted that the notional income to the extent of Rs. 3000/- per month should have been considered and the physical disability ought to have been considered as 60%.
7.

Since, the occurrence of the accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, driving licence, route permit and insurance policy etc. have not been disputed by the Learned Advocate representing the respondent No.1/insurance company, this Court restricts itself only to the extent of issues agitated by the respective parties.
8. The document marked as Ext.8 i.e. the disability certificate and 8/1 stated the physical disability to the extent of 80% to have been suffered by the victim as a consequence of the accident.
It further mentioned the age of the victim to be 32 at the time of the accident.

The document marked as Ext.
6/1 being the injury report as well as the document marked as Ext.4 being the voter ID Card stated the age of the victim to be 32 years at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the multiplier should have been considered to be 16 instead of 18.
The document marked as Ext. 11 series mentioned the final bill to have been issued by the Calcutta Medical Research Institute to the tune of Rs. 7,28,786/.

Since the victim could not prove his monthly income through document or corroborative evidence to the extent of an earning of Rs. 300 to 400 per day, considering the fiscal index prevalent in the year 2013 it would not be improbable if his monthly income is considered to Rs. 4000/-.
The learned Tribunal did not grant any compensation towards future prospect in the event of physical permanent disability to have been suffered by the victim to the extent of 80%.

9. Considering the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National insurance company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Shetty & Anr1 and Sarala Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.2 The impugned award of Rs. 9,49,786/- is modified as follows:

The appellant/claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs. 9,39,160/-
along with 1 2017(4)TAC 673(S.C) (2009) 6 SC 121 interest at the rate of 6%per annum to be paid from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of realization.
11.

The Learned Advocate for the respondent No.1/insurance company is to deposit the balance sum of Rs. 9,39,160/- along with interest before the office of the learned Registrar General High Court at Calcutta within six weeks from the date of passing of this order.

12. The office of the Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta shall encash the said cheque and,
thereafter, disburse the same to the present appellant/claimant as mentioned in the award passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Additional District Judge, Fast Track Court-II, Tamluk, Purba Medinipur in M.A.C. Case No. 100 of 2016 on proof of proper identification of the appellant /claimant subject to payment of ad valorem Court's fees within four weeks.
